title: AssetDrawer: no dialog role, no focus handling, focusable full-screen scrim
body:
## Summary
The Outputs shelf's asset drawer covers the page (fixed inset-0 z-50) but is not a dialog. It has no role=dialog or aria-modal and no accessible name. It does not move focus in, trap it, or hand it back. Its scrim is a full-screen <button aria-label="Close">, which is the exact pattern components/ui/Modal.tsx retired as an ARIA violation.

## Description
AssetDrawer.tsx:124-126: a <div className=fixed inset-0 z-50> holding <button aria-label="Close" className="absolute inset-0 ..."> and an <aside>. Nothing calls focus(). The only keyboard affordance is a window Escape listener (:117-121). A keyboard user who opens an asset from LibraryShelves stays focused on the card behind the scrim. Tab walks the page underneath, starting with a full-viewport 'Close' button, and closing does not return focus. Modal.tsx documents each of these: the scrim as a div because a focusable aria-hidden full-screen control is a violation (:263-270), focus into the panel (:214), the Tab trap (:172-195), and restoreFocus (:72-87). Two controls are both named Close ('Close', 'Close details', :125 and :141).

## Flow
- Studio > Outputs > press Enter on an asset card
- The drawer paints, but focus stays on the card under the scrim and a screen reader hears nothing about a dialog
- Tab: focus reaches the full-screen 'Close' scrim and then page controls behind the drawer

## Expected impact
The drawer behaves like every other overlay in the app: it is announced as a dialog named by the asset title, focus starts on its close control and is held inside, and closing returns focus to the card.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a keyboard/SR user can find, stay in, and leave the asset drawer
Before: Modal.tsx overlay guarantees present in AssetDrawer: 0/5 (role=dialog, aria-modal, name, focus-in/trap, restore). Focusable full-screen scrim: 1
After: 5/5. Scrim is a div aria-hidden
Method: probe - source read AssetDrawer.tsx:117-167 vs Modal.tsx:72-87,162-222,262-284
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_studio/AssetDrawer.tsx:117-121 (Escape only), 124-125 (<button aria-label="Close" className="absolute inset-0 bg-black/60">), 126 (<aside> with no role/aria-modal/label); components/ui/Modal.tsx:263-270 (the retired button-scrim note), 214, 220; consumer app/_library/LibraryShelves.tsx:171
verify: New tests/golden-path/asset-drawer-dialog.probe.spec.ts (stripComments source read of app/_studio/AssetDrawer.tsx). Assert: role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" on the panel, aria-labelledby pointing at the title h3's id, no <button whose className contains 'absolute inset-0' (the scrim becomes <div aria-hidden>), a focus() call in an effect (the close button or panel), and focus restored to the previous document.activeElement on cleanup, falling back to <main> the way Modal.restoreFocus does. A Tab trap may reuse Modal's selector list. Red on HEAD (0 of these), green after. Do not change LibraryShelves (other context). The drawer's props stay unchanged.

title: Why 'Lock step' is disabled is said only in a title on a disabled button
body:
## Summary
When a step cannot be signed off, the Lock step button gets `disabled` and the reason ('Nothing has been started on this step yet', 'Step is blocked and cannot be signed off') lives only in its native title. A disabled button is skipped by Tab, Firefox does not show a title tooltip on a disabled element, and the reason is not part of the accessible name or description. Keyboard and screen-reader users get a dimmed 'Lock step' with no way to learn why.

## Description
StudioView.tsx:353-373: disabled={!isLocked && Boolean(blocker)}, title={... blocker ...}, label 'Lock step'. signOffBlocker returns the reason (lib/projects.ts:670-671). handleSignOff already returns early when `blocker` is set (StudioView.tsx:249), so the button can stay focusable (aria-disabled) without a second guard. The repo's rule is that colour or position is never the only signal. Here the only signal of 'why' is a hover tooltip.

## Flow
- Open a project on a step with nothing started
- Tab across the title line: focus skips Lock step entirely
- With a screen reader, browse to it: 'Lock step, dimmed', no reason

## Expected impact
The blocker is reachable by keyboard and spoken: the button is aria-disabled with an aria-describedby to the blocker text (sr-only or a Hint glyph), and stays in the tab order.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the reason a step cannot be locked is reachable without a mouse
Before: channels carrying the blocker: 1 (title on a disabled element; keyboard 0, SR 0)
After: keyboard-reachable and in the accessible description
Method: probe - source read StudioView.tsx:353-373 and lib/projects.ts:668-672
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:356 (disabled=...blocker), 357 (title=blocker), 249 (handleSignOff guards blocker); lib/projects.ts:670-671 (the two blocker sentences, 8 words each)
verify: Extend tests/golden-path/step-sign-off.probe.spec.ts (it already covers sign-off) with a source test over stripComments(StudioView.tsx). The sign-off button (data-testid=studio-step-signoff) does not use the `disabled=` attribute for the blocker case. It carries aria-disabled and aria-describedby, and the referenced element renders {blocker}. Red on HEAD, green after. The blocker text is a fact about the work (≤ 8 words), so a visible <Hint variant="warn"> is also allowed. Keep the title if desired, since it is not the only channel after the fix. Then run npm run check:narration.

title: Storage door offers only the absent door's exit; its doctrine says it differs
body:
## Summary
StudioView keeps a 'storage' door separate from 'absent' 'because … the work is on disk and merely out of reach, and the thing to do about it is different'. The JSX then gives both doors the same and only action: 'back to your projects →'. The messages studioDb rejects with ('storage is open in another tab') describe a condition the user can clear, then retry here. Today that retry is a browser reload the screen never offers.

## Description
Door doctrine: StudioView.tsx:92-94. Absent branch: :405-427, Link 'back to your projects →'. Storage branch: :428-448, the same Link text and target, rose-tinted. The open effect (:119-159) runs only on [id, user, router], so nothing in the page can re-run getProject. studioDb's blocked rejection is lib/studioDb.ts:126. error.tsx, one file over, offers 'Try again' plus 'Reload' for the same kind of recoverable failure (app/error.tsx:100-105).

## Flow
- Open /studio/<id> while another tab holds the DB upgrade
- Rose card: 'storage is open in another tab', with one button back to /projects
- Close the other tab. The only way back into this project is the shelf, then the row again, or a manual reload

## Expected impact
The storage door does what its doctrine says. It adds a Try again (Button primitive) that re-runs the open, beside the existing way out, so the user can recover in place.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a recoverable storage failure can be retried where it happened
Before: distinct remedies between the absent and storage doors: 0 (identical Link)
After: 1 (storage adds a retry that re-runs getProject)
Method: probe - source read StudioView.tsx:92-94,405-448,119-159
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/studio/[projectId]/StudioView.tsx:92-94 ('the thing to do about it is different'), 421-426 vs 442-447 (same Link, same text), 159 (effect deps: no retry nonce); lib/studioDb.ts:126; app/error.tsx:100-105 (Try again + Reload precedent)
verify: New tests/golden-path/studio-door-retry.probe.spec.ts, a source read of stripComments(StudioView.tsx). The door-storage branch contains a control whose onClick re-runs the open: a `attempt` state in the open effect's deps that the button increments, with door reset to opening. The door-absent branch does not contain it. Red on HEAD, green after. Use <Button> from components/ui/Primitives, labelled 'Try again' to match app/error.tsx. Add no explanatory sentence.

title: StepDot: zero consumers, and paints 'done' cyan against emerald-done
body:
## Summary
assetParts.tsx exports StepDot, a status dot that draws done as bg-cyan-300 and running as bg-cyan-300/60 (two states, one hue). It has no consumer anywhere in the repo. Everywhere else done or locked is emerald (Stepper TONE.done, RaceSheet GATE.done, STATE_TONE.delivered), so it is a dead second spelling of the status language waiting to be reused.

## Description
app/_studio/assetParts.tsx:163-174 defines StepDot. `git grep -n StepDot` returns only the definition. The file header (:3-5) still advertises 'the step status dot'. Its palette contradicts app/studio/[projectId]/Stepper.tsx:125 (done emerald) and app/_projects/RaceSheet.tsx:82 (done emerald), and colour is its only channel (aria-hidden, no glyph), which the Stepper header calls the shape this repo forbids (Stepper.tsx:79-85).

## Flow
- None today. The first consumer to reach for it ships a cyan 'done' that is colour-only

## Expected impact
One less off-vocabulary status primitive, and the header comment stops advertising it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no status primitive in the tree spells 'done' in a different hue than the rest
Before: StepDot consumers: 0. Off-vocabulary done-hue primitives exported: 1
After: 0 and 0 (deleted, header line updated)
Method: gate - git grep -n StepDot ⇒ 1 line (definition only)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: $ git grep -n StepDot -> app/_studio/assetParts.tsx:164:export function StepDot(...) (only hit, no tests either); app/_studio/assetParts.tsx:3-5 header; Stepper.tsx:125 done=emerald; RaceSheet.tsx:82 done=emerald
verify: Delete StepDot (assetParts.tsx:163-174) and the `StepStatus` import if it becomes unused (check app/_studio/types.ts consumers). Drop 'and the step status dot' from the header. `git grep -n StepDot` must return 0 lines. npm run typecheck and npm run lint:ratchet green.

title: Stepper says its tone colours the title; the JSX colours only the mark
body:
## Summary
Stepper's TONE docstring says the state colour is 'applied to the mark AND the title, so the two read as one statement about one step rather than a chip beside a word'. The JSX applies TONE only to the mark's span. Titles are white or white/60 by selection alone. StudioView's header comment also still describes the rail as 'one row of numbers and titles', and the numbers were removed on 2026-09-09.

## Description
Stepper.tsx:122-123 (the claim) vs :201 (TONE on the mark span) and :204-206 (title: on ? text-white : text-white/60, no TONE). StudioView.tsx:12 ('the step rail is one row of numbers and titles') vs Stepper.tsx:77-85 (THE NUMBERS ARE GONE). On this repo comments are read as spec by later sessions. A builder 'fixing' the rail to the docstring would retint five titles, a visible design change nobody decided. A builder trusting the StudioView line would look for numerals.

## Flow
- A later session reads Stepper's TONE docstring as the spec and 'restores' tinted titles, or measures the rail against it and files a phantom regression

## Expected impact
The comments say what the rail draws, so the next change to the rail starts from the truth.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - (indirect) the next rail change is made against an accurate spec
Before: comment claims about the rail contradicted by its JSX: 2
After: 0
Method: probe - source read Stepper.tsx:122-123,201-206 and StudioView.tsx:12
Result: better
Gate: none
verify: Comment-only edit. Reword the TONE docstring to 'applied to the mark; selection, not state, sets the title's weight' and StudioView.tsx:12 to 'one row of titles, each with its state mark'. Do NOT retint titles, which is a design decision. `git diff` shows comment lines only, and npm run typecheck is green.

lens_checked.visual-craft: Read Stepper.tsx (TONE and StateMark per state, active rule), StudioView.tsx title line (spec chip, prototype stamp, Lock and Outputs pills), projectParts.tsx (CLIP_WORD/CUE_WORD, TimeRuler, LANE_GUTTER), assetParts.tsx (MockPreview, CaptionBlock, ProvenanceBlock, StepDot), AssetDrawer.tsx, against globals.css .scroll-x/.scroll-y and the emerald=done / amber=call / rose=blocked vocabulary. Filed: StepDot.
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Door states opening/open/absent/storage (StudioView.tsx:96-159, 405-448), rail pick plus park plus re-read (:186-214), ?step deep link vs live change (:216-242), Outputs disclosure closes on any rail click (:192), sign-off/reopen. Filed: storage door has no retry.
lens_checked.state-coverage: getProject resolve/absent/reject/blocked (lib/studioDb.ts:126 rejects, so 'opening…' cannot hang on a blocked upgrade). Sign-off/reopen/bookmark failures go to the bell via reportStorageTrouble (:211,254,264), which is deliberate. CaptionBlock written/pending/failed are three distinct branches. Outputs tally ASSETS.length is a fixture count covered by the unconditional 'prototype · mocked data' stamp (fixtures still feed cut/deriveTimeline.ts, research beats, script trailer, _library/LibraryShelves).
lens_checked.copy-auditor: Diffed every header comment against the JSX in StudioView/Stepper/phases/projectParts/assetParts/AssetDrawer. Filed: Stepper/StudioView rail drift. Checked CLIP_WORD failed→'rejected' vs CUE_WORD failed→'refused': clip 'failed' is set nowhere in app/_phases/frames (grep), so this is not a live two-names defect.
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: Stepper aria-current=step plus sr-only state word, StateMark aria-hidden, Outputs aria-pressed, Lock button, AssetDrawer overlay, CaptionBlock role=status (aria-label plus a duplicate sr-only text, minor, not filed), ProvenanceBlock parent buttons (text-labelled). Filed: AssetDrawer dialog semantics, Lock blocker unreachable.

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: The studio is a desktop production workspace (five-step rail, timeline lanes). No narrow-width contract is declared in these files.
